'''David Edgar Games''' (1938<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Langley|first=G. John|date=2020|title=Dai Games Special Issue|journal=Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry|language=en|volume=34|issue=S4|article-number=e8886|doi=10.1002/rcm.8886|issn=1097-0231|doi-access=free|pmid=32652670 }}</ref> &ndash; 28 May 2018)<ref>[https://funeral-notices.co.uk/notice/games/1822343 David Edgar Games]</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.southwalesargus.co.uk/news/16307877.tributes-paid-eminent-scientist-professor-david-dai-games-leaves-behind-a-great-legacy/|title=Tributes paid to eminent scientist Professor David 'Dai' Games who leaves behind 'a great legacy'|date=22 June 2018|website=South Wales Argus|access-date=26 May 2024}}</ref> was a Welsh chemist best known for his work in mass spectrometry and chromatography.

== Early life and education ==
Dai grew up in Ynysddu in South Wales and attended the Lewis School, Pengam.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jones|first=Jonathan J.|date=2020|title=Remembering Dai Games|journal=Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry|language=en|volume=34|issue=S4|article-number=e8889|doi=10.1002/rcm.8889|pmid=32657448 |issn=1097-0231|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
Dai graduated from [[King's College London]], where he also obtained his PhD. After postdoctoral work at [[McMaster University]], Hamilton, he moved to University of Wales Cardiff, where he progressed to a personal chair.  In 1989 he moved to Swansea as Head of the Mass Spectrometry Research Unit at University of Wales, Swansea. Although best known as a mass spectrometrist and separation scientist who was the first person to bring [[Liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry|liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry]] to Europe, he has made considerable contributions in organic chemistry research and served as Head of the Chemistry Department at Swansea.

== Awards and honours ==
In 1987, he was awarded the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] medal for Analytical Separations and in 1991, was awarded the Martin Medal by the [[Chromatographic Society]]. In 1993 he received the Gold Medal of the Society of Analytical Chemistry. The [[International Mass Spectrometry Society]] awarded him the J.J.Thomson Medal in 1997, and in 1999 he received the A.J.Evans Medal from Cardiff University.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Member Only Content {{!}} BMSS|url=https://www.bmss.org.uk/heritage/notable-names-in-british-ms/#dai-games|access-date=2021-04-08|website=www.bmss.org.uk}}</ref>

He was a past Chairman of the [[British Mass Spectrometry Society|BMSS]], served on the SERC Chemistry Committee as Chairman of the Instrumentation Panel and also on NERC, MRC and AFRC panels. He was a former Joint Editor-in-Chief of Biomedical and Environmental Mass Spectrometry.<ref name=":0" />
